answer: Orchard-splitting credit routing. Each agent earns routing credit only by relaying traffic across distinct, previously unlinked neighbor pairs; credit decays unless refreshed through fresh edges. An attacker must sustain real relay capacity on many disjoint edges, like planting a new orchard row per alias. Cost: provisioning and maintaining independent link bandwidth per fake identity, which scales linearly with alias count. A bridge node cannot reuse one path, and a meadow of idle aliases accrues no credit.
